results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the supplied basis, $N\ge1$, the lower bound $b$, real energies $\varepsilon_j\ge b$, and $\beta>0$ in clause (c).

[F1] Completed tensor products have dense algebraic tensor products and the elementary-tensor inner-product formula; the permutation projections are bounded orthogonal projections acting by finite permutation sums ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]).

[F2] In each finite prefix $H_m:=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}$ the Slater vectors indexed by $N$-element subsets form an orthonormal antisymmetric basis, and the orbit sums are a nonzero orthogonal symmetric basis ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (a)-(c)).

[F3] Cauchy-Schwarz controls square-summable coefficient pairings ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]). A complete orthonormal family gives Parseval and norm-convergent coordinate expansion ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]). The adjoint of a densely defined operator is characterized by $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$, and equality with the adjoint means self-adjointness ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

[F4] A PVM is strongly countably additive; integration of bounded Borel functions gives the corresponding bounded operator and its scalar spectral integrals ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). The unbounded identity integral has the scalar squared-moment domain and is obtained by bounded coordinate truncations ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F5] Finite-rank operators are compact and their operator-norm limits are compact ([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]). An absolutely summable nuclear series defines a trace-class operator, with trace equal to the sum of its rank-one traces; a trace-class operator has an absolutely summable diagonal in every supplied orthonormal basis ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).



**Proof technique:** direct; exhaust the supplied basis by finite prefixes, compute the unbounded diagonal adjoint on coordinates, and compare nonnegative fixed-N occupation sums.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Product basis and finite-prefix exhaustion] The tensors $e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ are orthonormal by [F1]. Their span is dense: approximate each factor of an elementary tensor by its finite basis truncation using [F3]; the tensor norm formula and the telescoping difference of two products show convergence of these approximations, and finite sums of elementary tensors are dense by [F1]. Every finite collection of words is contained in some $H_m^{\otimes N}$. Since each $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is bounded, its images of this dense word span are dense in its range. In the finite prefix, these images span precisely the finite Slater or orbit-sum basis of [F2]. A word in $\operatorname{orb}(n)$ uses only finitely many modes, and the orbit consists of distinct orthonormal product vectors, so its sum has norm squared $|\operatorname{orb}(n)|>0$. Thus its displayed normalization agrees in every larger prefix. The finite-prefix Slater vectors likewise agree in every larger prefix. Any pair of proposed occupation vectors lies in a common prefix, where [F2] gives orthogonality; the normalized vectors have norm one. Their span is dense in the sector by the projection argument, proving (a). The index sets are countable because they are countable unions of finite prefix index sets. [F1, F2, F3, algebra, construct]

2.1 [Diagonal domain and self-adjointness] Write either sector in the orthonormal coordinates of step 1.1. The specified domain contains every finite coordinate vector, hence is dense. For a vector in that domain, Parseval makes the defining energy series converge. If $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain, with adjoint value $z$, testing against each $b_c^\sigma$ gives $z_c=E_cy_c$ because $E_c$ is real. Since $z$ is square summable, $\sum_c|E_cy_c|^2<\infty$, so $y$ belongs to the specified domain. Conversely, if that sum is finite, Cauchy-Schwarz applied to the square-summable coefficient families gives $\langle H_N^\sigma x,y\rangle=\langle x,H_N^\sigma y\rangle$ for every domain vector $x$, so $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain with the stated value. The domains and values agree, proving self-adjointness by [F3]. Since every $E_c\ge Nb$, the absolutely convergent energy quadratic sum is at least $Nb\|x\|^2$. Finite coordinate truncations converge in both norm and graph norm since both square-sum tails vanish, so finite occupation sums are a core and the operator is their diagonal closure. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Labelled energy and spectral measure] The same coordinate-domain construction on the product-word basis defines a self-adjoint labelled operator with energies $\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k}$, agreeing with the free slot-energy sum on finite mode words. Every permutation of a word has the same energy, so its domain and action commute with each permutation unitary and the projections [F1]. Their sector restrictions have exactly the occupation energies and domain of step 2.1. For the displayed $E_N^\sigma(B)$, the projection and intersection identities follow coordinatewise; for disjoint $B_l$, the tails of the square-summable coordinates give strong countable additivity and total mass $I$, so it is a PVM. The scalar measure of a vector $\psi=\sum_ca_cb_c^\sigma$ is $\sum_c|a_c|^2\delta_{E_c}$, so [F4] gives the identity-integral domain exactly $\sum_cE_c^2|a_c|^2<\infty$; bounded spectral truncations converge to the displayed coordinate action there. This PVM is also uniquely determined by that operator: if another PVM represents it, the zero norm of $(H_N^\sigma-E_c)b_c^\sigma$ forces its scalar measure at $b_c^\sigma$ to be supported at $E_c$. Its projections therefore act as $\mathbf1_B(E_c)$ on every $b_c^\sigma$, and density gives equality on the whole sector. For the exponential, use the bounded Borel function $g(a)=e^{-\beta\max\{a,Nb\}}$ on $\mathbb R$; it agrees with $e^{-\beta a}$ on the support of this PVM. [F4] therefore gives the bounded positive operator with eigenvalues $e^{-\beta E_c}\le e^{-\beta Nb}$, namely $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$. This proves (b) and identifies the exponential used in (c). [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Extended trace and occupation sums] Put $r_c:=e^{-\beta E_c}$, a bounded positive family. In the supplied occupation basis the extended positive trace is $\sum_cr_c$. This value is basis independent even when infinite: if $(v_l)$ is any other orthonormal basis, then $\sum_l\langle e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}v_l,v_l\rangle=\sum_l\sum_cr_c|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=\sum_cr_c$, since nonnegative-series sums can be interchanged as suprema over finite subsums, and Parseval gives $\sum_l|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=1$. A Bose occupation sequence has a unique sorted word $i_1\le\cdots\le i_N$, and a Fermi subset has a unique increasing word; $e^{-\beta E_c}$ is the product of the corresponding $q_j$. Thus the trace equals $h_N(q)$ or $e_N(q)$ as stated. If the sum is finite, the series of rank-one operators $\sum_cr_c\langle\cdot,b_c^\sigma\rangle b_c^\sigma$ is nuclear and converges in operator norm to the exponential: its norm tail is at most the summable scalar tail. Its finite-rank partial sums and [F5] first give compactness, and the nuclear criterion then gives trace class and the ordinary trace formula. Conversely trace class forces the diagonal sum to be finite by [F5]. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Upper and lower bounds and finiteness] Let $Q:=\sum_jq_j\in(0,\infty]$. The sum over all ordered words of length $N$ is $Q^N$: on the first $m$ modes it is $(\sum_{j\le m}q_j)^N$, and every finite collection of words is contained in one such prefix. The nondecreasing and strictly increasing index sets are subsets of the ordered-word set, giving $Z_N^\sigma\le Q^N$. For $N\ge2$, configurations selecting modes $1,\ldots,N-1$ once each and one additional mode $j\ge N$ are valid for both statistics, distinct as $j$ varies, and have weight $(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k)q_j$. Their sum gives the lower bound. For $N=1$, every configuration is the single mode $j$, so both traces equal $Q$; the empty product is $1$ and the tail starts at $1$. For any $N$, the lower-bound coefficient is strictly positive and finite, and the omitted initial segment of $Q$ is finite. Hence $Q=\infty$ forces $Z_N^\sigma=\infty$, whereas $Q<\infty$ gives $Z_N^\sigma<\infty$ by the upper bound. The single configuration $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has positive weight for either sign, so both traces are strictly positive. This proves all of (c). No sum over particle numbers or full-Fock product formula is used. [step 4.1, given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The choice hypotheses, $A,E_A,\rho,\mu_\rho^A$, and in (c) the explicitly stated literal-product assumptions.

[F1] The density eigenexpansion has positive weights and orthonormal vectors, converges in trace norm, and gives $\mu_\rho^A(B)=\sum_kw_kE_{A,u_k}(B)$. For $u\in D(A)$, $\int a\,dE_{A,u}=\langle Au,u\rangle$; absolute first integrability alone is equivalent to $u\in D(|A|^{1/2})$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a)-(c)).

[F2] Nonnegative monotone limits commute with integrals, and integrable domination permits limits of signed integrals ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F3] Bounded Borel spectral integrals agree with their scalar spectral integrals ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Bounded multiplication of a density eigenexpansion gives $\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$ and bounded cyclicity gives $\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]]).

[F4] A trace-class operator has its trace as an absolutely convergent diagonal in a supplied Hilbert basis; it also has a nuclear representation whose rank-one traces sum to its trace ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]], [[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]]). Under AC, a chain of orthonormal families containing a given family has its orthonormal union as an upper bound, so [[thm-zorn]] provides a maximal extension. Its orthogonal complement is zero by maximality, hence it is complete by [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]. Coordinate expansion is [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]. Finite-rank maps and their operator-norm limits are compact ([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]).



**Proof technique:** direct; integrate the density eigenexpansion and compare it with correctly defined trace products.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [First-moment expansion] By [F1] the outcome measure is the countable weighted sum of the scalar measures. This gives $\int g\,d\mu_\rho^A=\sum_kw_k\int g\,dE_{A,u_k}$ first for nonnegative simple functions by the measure identity and finite linearity, and then for all nonnegative measurable $g$ by increasing simple approximation and [F2]; the nonnegative sums interchange as increasing finite subsums. Taking $g=|a|$ gives the first identity in (a), including infinity. When it is finite, both positive and negative parts are integrable, so subtracting their two finite sums gives $m=\sum_kw_k\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}$ with $\sum_kw_k|\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}|\le\sum_kw_k\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k}<\infty$. For each positive $w_k$, only absolute first integrability is forced; [F1] identifies its form domain, without requiring the operator-square moment. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Bounded observable] If $A$ is bounded, every $u_k$ is in $D(A)$, and Cauchy-Schwarz for the scalar probability measure gives $\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k}\le(\int a^2\,dE_{A,u_k})^{1/2}=\|Au_k\|\le\|A\|$ by [F1] ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]). Step 1.1 therefore bounds the first absolute moment by $\|A\|$. Each $u_k$ is in $D(A)$ and [F1] gives $\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}=\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$. Thus step 1.1 and the bounded trace formula [F3] give $m=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$. This proves (b). [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Literal trace-class left product] Under (c), $\rho u_k=w_ku_k\in D(A)$ and $w_k>0$, so each $u_k\in D(A)$ and $Tu_k=w_kAu_k$. Complete the orthonormal eigenfamily by an orthonormal basis of its perpendicular subspace using the already assumed AC. The density eigenexpansion shows $\rho=0$ on that perpendicular subspace, so $T=0$ there. The trace diagonal formula [F4] therefore gives $\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_k\langle Tu_k,u_k\rangle=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$. Step 1.1 and [F1] identify this absolutely convergent scalar sum with $m$. This proof uses the literal-product hypothesis to obtain $u_k\in D(A)$; it does not infer that hypothesis from first-moment existence. [F1, F4, step 1.1, choose, algebra]

3.1 [Closure of the right product] For $x\in D(A)$ and arbitrary $y$, self-adjointness of $A$ and $\rho$ gives $\langle\rho Ax,y\rangle=\langle Ax,\rho y\rangle=\langle x,A\rho y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle=\langle T^*x,y\rangle$, so $\rho A$ agrees with the bounded $T^*$ on the dense domain $D(A)$. Its graph closure is all of the graph of $T^*$: approximate any $x$ by $x_l\in D(A)$ and use boundedness of $T^*$, while its closed graph contains every graph limit from that restriction. A nuclear representation $T=\sum_jT_{v_j,z_j}$ gives $T^*=\sum_jT_{z_j,v_j}$ with the same summable nuclear norms; the operator-norm convergence of these finite-rank partial sums first gives compactness, and then the nuclear criterion gives trace class and [F4] gives $\operatorname{tr}(T^*)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(T)}=m$, since the spectral integral $m$ is real. This proves (c), without invoking cyclicity for unbounded multipliers. [F4, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

**Given:** the finite-mode non-interacting model data of the statement with its eigenbasis $(e_1,\dots,e_d)$, eigenvalues $\varepsilon_j$, sector projections $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$.

[F1] **Finite spectral theorem.** A self-adjoint endomorphism $h$ of the finite-dimensional complex inner product space $K$ is normal, so $K$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of $h$ with real eigenvalues ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] **Slot operators.** For $h\in\mathcal B(K)$ the slot operator $h^{(i)}$ acts on elementary tensors by $h^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes hv_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|h^{(i)}\|\le\|h\|$, and $(h^{(i)})^*=(h^*)^{(i)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

[F3] **Product basis and occupation bases.** The elementary tensors $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ over all multi-indices form an orthonormal basis of $K^{\otimes N}$; the Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_N})$ over $N$-element subsets $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(N)}$ with $e_J^\wedge$ zero-free for distinct indices and vanishing on repeated indices; the vectors $m_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$ over $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ form an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(N)}$, and $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$, $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F4] **Configuration counts.** The map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection from $N$-element subsets onto $\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$, the sector dimensions are $\binom dN$ and $\binom{N+d-1}{N}$, and for $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Stationary states.** For the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$, a nonzero $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ if and only if its pure preparation is stationary, and then $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c)); the outcome law of an assigned observable in a preparation is the trace law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), and the trace is basis independent ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).



**Proof technique:** direct; expand in the product basis of one-particle eigenmodes, transport the diagonal action to the two sector bases, and read the finite spectrum and trace.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The labelled operator on the product basis] By [F2] each $h^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$. On the product basis vector $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ the $i$-th slot operator acts as $h$ on the factor $e_{i_k}$, giving $h^{(k)}e_i=\varepsilon_{i_k}e_i$; hence $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k})e_i$. Since every $U_\pi$ permutes the slots and $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is the sum over all slots, $U_\pi H_{\mathrm{lab}}U_\pi^*=H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Partition sum and the zero sector] Normalize the symmetric vectors to $\widetilde m_\lambda:=m_\lambda/\|m_\lambda\|$; by [F3] these form an orthonormal eigenbasis, as do the Slater vectors in the fermionic sector. The trace is therefore $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$, with the configuration counts $M_N^-=\binom dN$ and $M_N^+=\binom{N+d-1}{N}$ from [F4]. For $\sigma=-$, $N>d$, the index set is empty and the trace is the empty sum $0$. There is no eigenvector on $\{0\}$ and hence no ground eigenvalue, and its only operator has trace $0$, so no trace-one density or normalized Gibbs density exists there. In every other case [F4] gives a finite nonempty index set, so its finite sum of positive Boltzmann weights has $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$. For that case finite minima and maxima $E_0,E_{\max}$ exist, and for each configuration $e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}\le e^{-\beta E_0}$, because $\beta>0$; summing the $M_N^\sigma$ inequalities proves the two bounds. This argument allows negative configuration energies. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. By [F5] and step 2.1 each such $\Psi$ is an eigenvector of the generator, so its pure preparation is stationary under the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ with $\Psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\Psi$, and the energy law of any preparation is the finite spectral law in the sector basis. This proves (d). [F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Extreme energies and ground eigenspace] Work on a nonzero sector. For $\sigma=-$, each configuration selects $N$ distinct eigenvalues, so its energy is at least the sum of the $N$ smallest and at most the sum of the $N$ largest; these bounds are attained by the corresponding subsets. Thus $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and $E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)}$. A minimizing subset contains every mode with energy strictly below $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, contains no mode with energy strictly above $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, and fills its remaining places with modes at that boundary energy; this includes all choices allowed by degeneracy. For $\sigma=+$, the identity $\sum_j\lambda_j=N$ gives $N\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\le N\varepsilon_{(d)}$; the two bounds are attained by putting all particles in a minimum-energy or maximum-energy mode respectively. Equality at the lower bound holds exactly when every occupied mode has energy $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally expand a unit vector in the orthonormal sector basis of step 3.1: $\psi=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$, $\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2=1$. Then $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle-E_0=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2(\lambda_\lambda-E_0)\ge0$, with equality exactly when all coefficients at energies greater than $E_0$ vanish, that is, exactly on the ground eigenspace. Together with step 3.1 this proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2] ∎



- **Basis independence.** The eigenvalues $\lambda_J$ and $\lambda_\lambda$ depend on the eigenvalue list of $h$, not on the choice of eigenbasis; a degenerate one-particle eigenvalue contributes with its multiplicity through the distinct configurations.
- **Fermionic emptiness.** For $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is zero: the algebraic partition trace is $0$, while there are no sector states, no ground eigenvalue and no normalized density. The observable and stationarity readings of clause (d) apply only to nonzero sectors.
- **Energy reference.** The bounds in (c) permit arbitrary real one-particle energies. If all configuration energies are nonnegative, then $Z_N\le M_N^\sigma$; this count-only upper bound is not valid for unrestricted negative energies. Shifting every one-particle energy by $a\in\mathbb R$ multiplies $Z_N$ by $e^{-\beta Na}$ and shifts both extreme energies by $Na$.

**Given:** the declared finite-dimensional sector model with energy operator $H_N^\sigma$, eigen-decomposition and parameters $\beta$, $T$, $k_B$; the canonical preparation $\rho_\beta$ and the functional $F$ of the statement.

[F1] **Supplied finite Gibbs data.** For the finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H_N^\sigma$ with eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_D)$, and $\beta>0$: $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty)$, $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=Z_N^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$, and for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ge-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$ with $s(\rho)\le\log D$ and equality $s(\rho)=\log D$ exactly for $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Spectral decomposition of a preparation.** A density operator $\rho$ on the finite-dimensional space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ has the form $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Dw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ with $w_i\ge0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $(u_i)$ an orthonormal eigenbasis, by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] applied as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a); with $p_{ij}:=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$ one has $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_ip_{ij}=1$, because $(u_i)$ and $(v_j)$ are orthonormal bases.

[F3] **Exact scalar logarithm suppliers.** For $x>0$, $\log'(x)=1/x$ and $\log x=\int_1^xdt/t$ ([[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]]); $\log$ is continuous, $\log1=0$ and $\log(x/y)=\log x-\log y$ for $x,y>0$ ([[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). For a continuous real function on $[a,b]$ differentiable on $(a,b)$, $a<b$, there is $\xi\in(a,b)$ with $f(b)-f(a)=f'(\xi)(b-a)$ ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]). The strict tangent bound and its equality case are derived below from these statements, rather than assumed from a strict Jensen theorem.



**Proof technique:** direct; express the free-energy difference as a sum of nonnegative scalar defects over the two orthonormal bases, with the zero-weight convention made explicit; the strict logarithm tangent bound determines the equality case, including degenerate Gibbs eigenspaces.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [The canonical preparation and its data] By [F1], $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is a finite sum with $0<Z_N<\infty$; since $D\ge1$ each term is positive, so $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N>0$ with $\sum_jq_j=1$. By [F1] the operator $\rho_\beta=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, hence a declared sector preparation of the model, and the two displayed identities are the clauses of [F1] together with the entropy definition. This proves (a). [F1, algebra]

1.2 [Strict scalar defects, including zero weights] By [F3] and the mean value theorem applied to $\log$ between $1$ and $t>0$, $t\ne1$, one has $\log t=(t-1)/\xi$ with $\xi$ strictly between $1$ and $t$; for $t>1$ this is less than $t-1$, and for $0<t<1$ it is also less than $t-1$ because the numerator is negative and $\xi<1$. Thus $\log t\le t-1$, with equality exactly at $t=1$. For $w\ge0$, $r>0$ define $b(w,r):=w\log(w/r)$ when $w>0$ and $b(0,r):=0$, and $d(w,r):=b(w,r)-w+r$. If $w>0$, apply the bound to $t=r/w$ and the quotient law to get $d(w,r)\ge0$, with equality exactly at $w=r$; if $w=0$, $d(0,r)=r>0$. Likewise $h(q,r):=\log r+(q-r)/r-\log q\ge0$ for $q,r>0$, with equality exactly at $q=r$, by applying the bound to $t=q/r$. [F3, algebra]

1.3 [The degenerate case] If $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ then $E_j=c$ for all $j$ and [F1] gives $Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $q_j=D^{-1}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$; by [F1] $s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log(De^{-\beta c})=c-k_BT\log D$. This proves (d). [F1, algebra]

2.1 [The free-energy difference for every mixed preparation] Let $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be as in [F2] and put $p_{ij}=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$, $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j$. Each $r_i>0$ and $\sum_ir_i=\sum_jq_j\sum_ip_{ij}=1$. Use the entropy convention $\eta(w)=w\log w$ for $w>0$ and $\eta(0)=0$ (the notation $0\log0=0$ does not define $\log0$). The trace pairing and the entropy definition give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)=\sum_{i,j}w_ip_{ij}E_j$ and $s(\rho)=-\sum_i\eta(w_i)$. Since $\beta E_j=-\log q_j-\log Z_N$, $\Delta:=\beta(F(\rho)-F_{\mathrm{eq}})=\sum_i\bigl(\eta(w_i)-w_i\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j\bigr)$. Define $a_i:=\log r_i-\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j=\sum_jp_{ij}h(q_j,r_i)$, the last equality using $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_jp_{ij}(q_j-r_i)=0$. Step 1.2 gives $a_i\ge0$, with equality exactly when $q_j=r_i$ for every $j$ with $p_{ij}>0$. By the quotient law for positive $w_i$ and by the explicit zero convention otherwise, $\Delta=\sum_i b(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i=\sum_i d(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i$, because $\sum_i(w_i-r_i)=0$. All summands are nonnegative, so $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, proving (b) for every density operator, including those with zero eigenvalues. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Equality, strict zero-weight exclusion and degeneracies] If $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, the finite sum of nonnegative defects in step 2.1 vanishes. Hence $d(w_i,r_i)=0$ for every $i$; step 1.2 gives $w_i=r_i>0$, since $d(0,r_i)=r_i>0$ excludes every zero weight. Thus $w_i a_i=0$ forces $a_i=0$ for every row, and step 2.1 gives $q_j=r_i=w_i$ whenever $p_{ij}>0$. In the expansion of $u_i$ in the orthonormal basis $(v_j)$, the coefficients at all $q_j\ne w_i$ therefore vanish, so $\rho_\beta u_i=w_i u_i$. Since also $\rho u_i=w_i u_i$ and $(u_i)$ is a basis, the two operators agree: $\rho=\rho_\beta$. This argument allows arbitrary changes of basis within any repeated-eigenvalue Gibbs eigenspace. Conversely $\rho=\rho_\beta$ gives equality by [F1]. Together with step 2.1, this proves (c) with no full-rank assumption on the competing preparation. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 prove (b) and (c), and step 1.3 proves (d). The argument is an optimisation inside the declared finite-dimensional sector at the adopted ensemble parameters; no equilibration, rate, thermodynamic limit or measured thermal quantity entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 3.1] ∎



- **Why the minimiser is unique.** The equality analysis shows that a minimiser must be diagonal in the same eigenbasis with the same weights; it excludes the block-diagonal counterexample in which $\rho$ is diagonal in a different basis, because equal weights on a degenerate eigenspace reassemble the same projector.
- **The adopted part.** The minimum property is a theorem about the functional; that a physical sample is described by $\rho_\beta$ remains the adopted assumption of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]], not a consequence of the optimisation.
